name: Copperplate Engraving
desc: An old-master burin plate: a draped ovoid volume modelled entirely out of line — swelling hatch ribbons that bend to follow the surface they describe, cross-hatched to solid black in the shadow and thinning to bare paper on the lit crown, the drapery folds breathing while a raking studio lamp crawls slowly around the form.

energy.doc: relief depth of the form under the raking lamp — at max the modelling is brutal and the darks go solid

scale.doc: size of the draped volume + hatch pitch

density.doc: number of hatch lines + burin flicks

weight.doc: line weight — hairline to fat solid burin

speed.doc: how fast the lamp rakes across the plate

style.doc: burin: bistre ink on toned laid paper · mezzotint: light scraped out of a velvet-black ground · sanguine: red chalk on toned buff · contour: uniform hairlines, no tone at all — the form as pure schematic line

act.doc: plate: steady · proof: the lamp orbits fast, pulling the form through every angle · burnish: the plate is reworked, tone deepening with the section arc

seed.doc: deterministic seed — same number, same piece
